purpose: Single authority for CYNIC-owned process supervision: roles, process model, lifecycle, signals, restart/backoff, health, privilege, observation, and hardware/OS portability. This document declares policy; it does not build, install, spawn, or execute anything.

authority.justification: Supervision is a stable cross-crate boundary: it constrains runtime baskets, capability privilege, CLI surfaces, host adapters, and service-manager projections. It is not a broad contract forest; it is the one contract that keeps those surfaces from drifting.

applies_to: child processes spawned by CYNIC-owned services
observation and bounded lifecycle actions over those processes

architecture.ownership: Supervision is one named responsibility with one owner. It is distinct from the operator CLI, domain logic, and protocol types.
architecture.pure_decision: Supervision decisions such as admit, restart, drain, degrade, and observe are pure functions and data with zero I/O. Spawn, signal, socket, and filesystem effects belong to imperative-shell adapters.
architecture.single_binary: CYNIC uses one canonical composition root. A role is selected by argv, not by shipping another binary.
architecture.foreground: All CYNIC processes run foreground. SysV double-fork and self-daemonization are prohibited. The host supervisor, such as systemd, remains the outer lifecycle owner.
architecture.portability: The architecture is OS/hardware-agnostic. OS-specific behavior is isolated behind cfg-gated adapters and typed platform boundaries. An OS is implemented only when a real use exists, but the architecture must not block future hosts.

process_model.parent: The CYNIC supervisor is an explicit process, not an implicit side effect of an operator command.

child_roles.note: Kernel lifecycle is boot-sensitive; it may be supervised by the host supervisor before CYNIC-owned observation is available.

MCP remains a projection boundary. The supervisor must not add a Cargo dependency from cynic-mcp to any crate; spawning an existing projection binary is permitted only while that constitutional boundary stands.

process_model.stdin: inherit or an explicit typed descriptor; never shell
process_model.stdout_stderr: inherit or route to a durable log adapter; never interpreted as protocol
process_model.process_group: Each child gets a process group where the platform supports it. Unix supervision must kill the process group, not only the direct child.
process_model.orphan_policy: An orphaned CYNIC-owned child is adopted by identity or reaped by explicit read-back. It is never silently ignored.

transitions.requires: typed role, argv, privilege, and capability admission
read-back that the process exists and, where declared, health passes
bounded drain, flush, and exit read-back
observed exit failure or health failure
missing or contradictory evidence; unknown is explicit, never fabricated as active

reload.requires: typed configuration reload and post-reload read-back

lifecycle.read_back: Every start, stop, restart, and degrade action requires observed process state or health evidence. A successful exit code alone is not proof.

health.failure: Unknown health is reported as unknown with residual unknowns. It is never coerced into active or stopped.

privilege.rule: Privilege is per capability and per admitted argv, never per binary. A supervisor spawn must not widen privilege.
privilege.sudoers: When installed, one generated membrane is preferred over ad-hoc bridge binaries. Shell execution is prohibited. The capability catalog remains the authority for privileged exec.

observation.journal: Capability id, resolved argv, exit code, and evidence id are recorded around every process event so an interrupted action remains attributable.

portability.implementation_policy: Build a host adapter only when a real use exists. The architecture must not block Linux, macOS, Windows, or future hardware, but no adapter is built speculatively.

phases: bounded start/stop for node with read-back

open_decisions.question: Should the CYNIC supervisor spawn existing daemon roles first, or absorb their internal child supervision immediately?
open_decisions.recommendation: spawn existing daemon roles first, then absorb internal supervision after proof

open_decisions.question: Should systemd remain the outer supervisor, or should CYNIC replace it?
open_decisions.recommendation: systemd remains the outer supervisor; CYNIC owns CYNIC-owned children and observations

ratification.why: The operator assumed the supervisor design for the sovereign OS direction and approved a contract-first migration. This contract is the single source before any supervisor code is written, so implementation cannot invent policy that has not been declared.
